newsitem.title: CHINA: China "move west" cotton project starts up.
newsitem.headline: China "move west" cotton project starts up.

text.p: The first project under a scheme to move some of China's cotton textile production from the east of the country to the western region of Xinjiang has begun operations, the Wen Hui Bao newspaper said on Saturday.
The Xinshen Textile Company, in the Xinjiang city of Shihezi, began production on Friday.
It is a joint venture of the Shanghai Number One Cotton Factory and the Xinjiang Shihezi Number Two Woollen Factory, and has a total investment of 58.896 million yuan, the paper said.
The Shanghai factory holds 51 percent of the venture and has moved 30,000 cotton spindles to the Shihezi plant, it said.

China is encouraging textile producers in the east to move their technology and equipment to Xinjiang, the country's biggest cotton producer, as a way to cut production costs and stimulate Xinjiang's less developed economy.
One other Shanghai factory is setting up a similar joint venture cotton textile plant in the Xinjiang city of Hami, the newspaper said.
The Shanghai Textile Group is also setting up a long-staple cotton production base in the Xinjiang areas of Turfan and Akesu, it said without elaborating.
